title: Two families, six boats, one very long group plan
notice: Fictional conversation for local CubeChat testing. People, vessels, headcounts, amounts, dates, payments and bookings are invented. This is not navigation, passenger-capacity, weather or passage advice; the possible Hawaii voyage is not an approved itinerary.

threatModel.motivation: The extended families include journalists and affluent financial professionals who worry that exposed payment instructions, passenger movements and meeting times could enable targeted interference or fraud.
threatModel.initialProvisioning: Ben has shared CubeChat and the matching directional secret material privately with Nora before the first exchange. Provisioning material is not part of the conversation or the intercepted traffic.
threatModel.exerciseScope: Controlled known-plaintext messaging and passive-capture exercise. The characters' desire for private coordination is not a claim that this experimental prototype provides production security.

A.name: Nora Hart
A.description: Seattle friend and informal point of contact for the Hart family; Leah Hart's cousin.

B.name: Ben Mercer
B.description: Bellevue friend and informal point of contact for the Mercer family; Owen Mercer's cousin.

stages.title: May 10 · The wedding becomes a sailing plan
June 5 · Four boats become five, then six
June 12 · The shared pot and the loose itinerary
August 1 · Mom wants to change the third
August 3 · Groceries, fuel and a corrected receipt
August 8 · Two boats consider what comes next

messages.text: Your CubeChat handoff worked; I have the directional files you gave me Saturday. Now, did your dad actually mean a trip down the coast, or was Leah and Owen's wedding toast just enthusiasm? Apparently we're one enormous sailing committee.

Actual trip. Glad the app and private key-file handoff worked; comparing the fingerprints in person was worth the extra coffee. Dad called from Bellevue with three spreadsheets. You and I are the family points of contact. Congratulations.
Excellent. I accept payment in coffee. Seattle side currently has Cedar Wake, Blue Lantern and Juniper interested. Is Second Wind definitely coming?
Yes. Four boats for now. I've got Cedar Wake 10, Second Wind 8, Blue Lantern 8, Juniper 8: 34 people. That's the overnight list, not everyone who clicked maybe.

Good, because Mom's version is already 'about fifty.' These are the larger family boats, but every skipper still needs to confirm their own actual berths and crew before anyone promises a cousin a bed.
I'll collect a yes or no from each boat. We're relaying family decisions, not telling six skippers how to sail. Dad was clear about that part, fortunately.
Rough idea is leave Seattle around July 15, work down the coast, and let people join or leave at planned shore stops. Nobody is signing up for an ocean crossing by agreeing to the family trip.
Thank you. Owen has already said Hawaii in front of three uncles. I'll translate that to 'possible later trip for two boats, separate decision.'

I'm glad we're trying a private planning channel. With the journalists on my side and the finance people on yours, a forwarded itinerary could expose rather more than our sandwich preferences. We can each pass the agreed version to our family.

Exactly. Some relatives are well off and some have sensitive reporting work. They worry someone could use our payment requests and meeting times to interfere. Questions here, dated decisions back to the families, and no public passenger schedule.
Fleet update: Tide Thread is in. Eight aboard, joining us in Seattle before departure. So five boats and 42 people now.
And North Starling? Mom has assigned them fruit already, which feels premature for a boat that hasn't said yes.
They just confirmed. Eight more, but they'll meet us at Port Townsend instead of Seattle. Six boats and 50 once they join. We don't have fifty squeezed onto the first four.
Updated: four = 34, five = 42, six = 50. Twenty-six on the Hart list and twenty-four on the Mercer list, including partners and friends. Leah and Owen only counted once each!
Skippers have confirmed those six boat lists. Please keep the people assigned to boats instead of letting everyone swap beds through the cousins' chat. Changes need to get back to both of us.

Will do. Food allergies go privately to the cooks. Work calendars and reporting contacts stay out of the trip lists altogether. Aunt Ruth can share holiday photos without attaching everyone's exact movements.
One more thing: Ruth and David are still talking as if 'we all go together' means six boats moving at identical speed. Can you untangle that with your dad?
Yes. Shared meeting places and check-ins; each skipper makes their own departure decision. If someone waits, we adjust the shore plans. Dinner reservations don't get a vote on weather.
Can we settle the money before Mom buys provisions for an expedition? Proposed coastal pot is $30,000. By our 26/24 split that's Hart $15,600 and Mercer $14,400.

That matches mine. Family contributions are in the trip ledger now, total $30,000. Let's hold $10,000 as a reserve and record every draw against a receipt. Offshore costs get a different budget later.

Shared meals and agreed group dock charges from the pot. Fuel recorded by boat, then reimbursed only where we agreed it was a group expense. Personal flights, shopping and repairs stay with the person or boat.

Fine. Dad's finance colleagues are especially worried about a fake 'send it here instead' message during the trip. Any payment change gets a call on the number we already know. Amounts and receipts here; bank details stay in the separate payment process.

Loose coast list from the skippers: Astoria, Newport, Coos Bay, Eureka, San Francisco area, then Monterey and perhaps Santa Barbara or San Diego. That's a list to work from, not a promise of arrival dates.
Dad says yes, subject to actual conditions and berths. He wants us to stop booking things that can't move. Jack is the tricky one because he has to fly back for work in early August.
Put Jack's work deadline on the list and give him a shore fallback. His office calendar can't become everyone's sailing deadline.
He agrees. He'll leave the boat early if needed and finish the airport journey by land. I think he's more worried about leaving his laptop charger aboard than missing the family barbecue.
Morning count in Seattle is five boats, 42 people. Tide Thread arrived last night. Mom brought enough muffins for fifty anyway, so North Starling's eight are represented in baked goods.
North Starling has the Port Townsend meeting update. I've got their skipper's acknowledgment. Can each boat send you its actual headcount before it leaves, rather than 'everyone is here' ?
Already collecting them. I also put copies of the shore arrangements with the boat leads so a phone losing signal doesn't mean nobody knows where the rental is.

Good. This is still our controlled CubeChat test, not a security guarantee. The skippers have their own working communication and emergency arrangements. If this drops out we use the agreed backup; silence doesn't mean everyone is fine.
North Starling is with us now. All six skippers checked their lists: Cedar Wake 10; the other five 8 each. Full coastal group is 50.
Confirmed on my side too. Leah and Owen haven't even finished sending their wedding thank-yous and already have a six-boat family event. They owe us another wedding cake.
Small meal-label correction: Tim was always assigned to Juniper, but his bag said Cedar Wake. No one is changing boats and those headcounts still stand. I fixed the food delivery label.
Thanks. I'll tell Dad before he sends Tim's dinner across the wrong dock. Next update after the skipper check-in; the coastal stops are still flexible.

Mom wants to know if on the 3rd we can do Half Moon Bay instead of Monterey. She says it would make the big shore shop easier and give the grandparents a quieter day. Is your side attached to Monterey?
Not attached, but which third? August 3, Tuesday, yes? Dad has a printout where Monterey is still penciled in for the 4th.
Yes, Tuesday August 3. Half Moon Bay, with the boats at Pillar Point if the skippers and berth arrangements allow it. Monterey moves later. Please recycle the printout with the coffee stain.
That could work for Jack too. He's looking at a flight home from San Jose on the 4th. San Jose is the airport run inland, not where we're putting the boats.
Good distinction. Mom just wrote 'meet in San Jose' and three people thought we had found a new marina. I'll say Pillar Point for the boats, San Jose for shopping and airport errands by car.
I'll ask all six skippers about the stop, then check the shore arrangements. Keep it proposed until I send the actual yeses. Dad can take Tim and Elias on the grocery run if we settle there.

Tell David that 'groceries' includes six boats' lists, not six carts of whatever looks nice. We need fresh food split by boat, cold items kept together, and no mystery crate for everyone to argue about.

Six skipper yeses now, subject to their final checks. Berth and rental arrangements confirmed in our trip sheet. Revised plan is Half Moon Bay on Aug 3; Monterey stays tentative for Aug 6. If we slip, Jack goes ashore sooner.
Passed that exact version to the Harts. Mom is happy. Please tell your side this replaces the earlier Aug 3 Monterey message, not adds a second place we're somehow attending simultaneously.
Done. Jack has a changeable flight and a land backup. I have removed the phrase 'we'll definitely be there' from Dad's draft. He's calling this excessive editing.

All six boats checked in at the stop. David, Tim and Elias will collect the rental this morning, shop from the combined list, then bring everything back to the docks. Who is receiving your side's bags?
Leah and I. Label bags with boat names before loading the car, please. Each boat sends someone to collect and stow its own food. We'll keep the cold bags moving first.
Fuel is separate from the grocery run: boat leads handle their own restock and send actual quantities and receipts. Dad has finally stopped asking whether the rental can bring fuel for everybody too.
Perfect. Today's dinner is still fifty. Jack leaves tomorrow, so the next meal order becomes forty-nine. Please don't remove him early; he will absolutely notice if his last dinner disappears.

They're back. Tim sorted the bags, Elias has the dock cart, Dad has the receipts. Can you send the boat people down now? And someone rescue Elias before he volunteers to carry all the potatoes himself.

On our way. Cedar Wake and Blue Lantern are taking their crates first, then Juniper. The others have their leads coming too. Nobody leaves the dock thinking a box marked 'shared' has magically stocked their galley.
Receipt check: your grocery total says $1,970, but there's a $120 produce receipt photographed twice. Is that one purchase or two? I haven't reimbursed the duplicate.

One purchase. Tim uploaded it and Dad sent it again. Correct groceries to $1,850. Dock charges $1,260 and agreed pooled fuel $2,140. Those are all the coastal-pot expenses posted so far; earlier personal purchases stayed personal.
Corrected ledger: $1,850 + $1,260 + $2,140 = $5,250 spent. From $30,000 that leaves $24,750. Holding the $10,000 reserve means $14,750 available for further agreed coastal costs.

Matches mine. I'll pass on the summary, no payment details. Keeping the rental overnight for Jack's airport run is on his personal tab; he already agreed. Dad returns it after dropping him off tomorrow.
Jack's packed and off Cedar Wake with his bags. Is David collecting him at the same dock entrance? He has asked me twice whether he can still make coffee before leaving.
Same entrance. Dad drives Jack to San Jose airport, drops him first, then returns the rental and uses the arranged ride back to Pillar Point. Tim and Elias are staying with the boats today.
Got it. Jack has his charger, work bag and shoes, which he apparently thinks are three separate milestones. I've marked him ashore, so aboard count is now forty-nine.
Meal count updated to 49 here too. David is only away for the errand, so he stays on tonight's list. Jack is the only person actually leaving the trip today.
Jack says he's through security. Dad returned the car and is back with us. Airport handoff complete. Nobody needs to keep holding the dock cart for a man who is now buying airport sandwiches.
Excellent. The remaining forty-nine are still on for the next coastal section when the skippers are ready. Mom wants another family dinner, but we can decide the restaurant after we know the stop.
And can we ask who is actually serious about Hawaii? People keep saying 'we're going' when they mean 'I'd like to visit while you're there.' Those are very different grocery lists.
I'll get a real answer. Only Cedar Wake and Second Wind are candidates. The other four are staying coastal, with their own berth and return arrangements. Nobody is committed to crossing by default.

Offshore interest list is back: four on Cedar Wake, four on Second Wind, including us. Eight total. The other forty-one still aboard plan to finish their family segment ashore before any offshore departure.

So of our original fifty, Jack is already home, forty-one more will leave, and eight might continue. Forty-two ashore overall. I'll keep the family meal orders at forty-nine until those forty-one actually disembark.

Exactly. The four coastal boats have separate arrangements after that; we aren't stranding them or borrowing their crews. I'll check every person's ride or flight before we mark the family segment finished.

Once Cedar Wake and Second Wind are down to four each, they can clear the family luggage and plan their own stores. We shouldn't buy ocean-passage food while every spare locker still contains somebody's wedding outfit.

The two skippers want a separate readiness review, crew agreement and current weather planning before choosing any departure point or window. If either boat isn't ready, Hawaii stays an idea. No date promised.

And a separate eight-person provision and fuel budget. Close out the coastal receipts first and return or agree the unused family money. The $24,750 balance isn't permission to spend everyone else's reserve on our adventure.

Agreed. That balance is still the Aug 3 posted figure; later receipts need reconciling before refunds. Each of the eight will approve the offshore costs separately. No automatic transfer from the family pot.

Mom asked whether 'Hawaii and back' means we'll be home by a particular Sunday. I told her the return needs its own plan and suitable window too. We can't book a round-trip ocean crossing like a ferry ticket.

Good. Family coast trip first; eight people and two boats can consider Hawaii afterward, with the return planned separately. I'll send that wording to the Mercers so nobody orders a welcome-home cake yet.
Harts have the same version now. Six boats, fifty people, one corrected produce receipt, and nobody accidentally signed up to cross the Pacific. I think we've earned that coffee.
